note: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl -> runs/theory-tests/s3/T1.jsonl (500 rows, one per problem). v3_last = rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text), the function grader/rln4_grader_v3.py calls; text includes the 3-token cue ' line!\n\nOkay'. First marker: the earliest of (a) the first line whose left-stripped text starts with 'Answer:' (case-sensitive; '**Answer:**', 'Final Answer:' and mid-line 'Answer:' do not count) and (b) the first '\boxed{'. first_score = grade_v3(gold, 'Answer: ' + content). Edge cases: an empty 'Answer:' line is still the first marker and scores 0; an unbalanced first '\boxed{' (only possible near the end of a capped text) scores 0; box content with a newline is graded only up to that newline because v3 reads a marker's rest of line. ALT reading: first marker = the earliest candidate under grader v3's own candidate set (MARK_V3 anywhere in a line with a non-empty rest, which includes 'Final Answer:', 'Answer is' and mid-line 'Answer:', or the first balanced box), graded the same way. At least one stored row (problem 54) ends '...0.15.Answer: 0.15' in the middle of a line, so the two readings can differ. RISK: grader v3's equivalence needs math_verify (plus numpy, which is stubbed if missing because it is only used in annotations). This laptop's python3 has no math_verify, so in this environment the script prints not_computable.

Same file, first-marker definition and grading as p1; all 500 rows, cap hits included. Discordant rows: first_score != v3_last. Main = discordant rows with first_score 1 / discordant rows; no discordant rows prints refuted with measured null. ALT = the same ratio with p1's alternative first marker (grader v3's own candidate set). Rows with no marker have first_score 0, so a row with no line-start 'Answer:' and no box that v3 grades right (e.g. through a mid-line 'Answer:' or 'Final Answer:') counts as discordant first-wrong/last-right. That pushes the main number down, and the ALT reading removes most of it. Needs math_verify, as in p1.

Before the run it held 2,137 rows: 2,000 attempt-0, 90 attempt-1 and 47 attempt-2, with no duplicate (problem, sample, attempt). Filter attempt == 0; the denominator is the attempt-0 rows present. v3_last = stored score_v3 (int 0/1 in every row). first_score as in p1. Statistic = (sum first_score - sum score_v3) / n. ALT = the same with p1's alternative first marker. Possible mismatch: the stored score_v3 was computed by the job's grader. If that grader differs from the current rln4_lib.grade_v3, the difference is built into the net gain, because first_score uses the current code. Needs math_verify.

File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl, fetched to runs/theory-tests/day1_3/<job>/answers.jsonl. Before the run it held 2,041 rows: 2,000 attempt-0, 32 attempt-1 and 9 attempt-2. Same computation as p3; refuted_by = measured > 0.004. RL's prompt asks for an 'Answer:' line. If RL writes a box early, for example in a mid-solution check, and its final answer on a later 'Answer:' line, the first marker is that early box, which can make the net negative. If RL writes only a mid-line 'Answer:' or a '**Answer:**' line, the main reading finds no marker and gives 0, which also makes the net negative. Neither case can push the number above 0.004 unless first-marker answers are right where the last one is wrong. ALT = v3-candidate first marker. Needs math_verify.

File: T1.jsonl as in p1. Filter: cap_hit is False and a first marker exists (p1's definition). End of the first marker: for an 'Answer:' line, the position of its newline (or the end of text); for a box, just after the matching brace (the end of text if unbalanced). Kept: text[end:] longer than 300 characters (the newline after an 'Answer:' line counts as one of them) AND (a line that starts at or after end and whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:', or '\boxed{' anywhere in text[end:]). Statistic = kept rows with recomputed grade_v3 == 0 / kept rows; no kept rows prints refuted. ALT reading, from the experiment text's 'answers with more than 300 characters': the whole answer longer than 300 characters instead of the text after the first marker, with the same further-marker condition. Caveat: a common base layout 'Answer: X' followed by '\boxed{X}' is kept only when more than 300 characters follow the first marker, so benign restatements can be counted too. Needs math_verify.
